purpose: Historical legally documented monetary outcomes, not a measure of toxic harm, fault, mortality or an additive company score.

USD.method: US CPI-U all items, U.S. city average, annual mean (NSA); reference 2025. 2025 BLS annual average omits October due to the federal funding lapse.

BRL.method: IBGE IPCA calendar-year Dec/Dec rates compounded after nominal base year through December 2025. The 2021 agreement was signed in February; December-2021 convention is only a standardized comparator, not a contractual indexation calculation.

cases.hazard: Mine-tailings dam failure / watershed and communities
cases.disposition: Judicial agreement; separate individual and criminal proceedings remain distinct

obligation.kind: Total agreed collective reparation package; includes works performed, future work and transfers

payment.detail: Minas Gerais environmental authority reported R$18.2bn already paid toward different agreement obligations after one year; covers multiple payment/implementation periods. This is a dated historical lower bound, not a current 2026 total. Separately, Vale's June 2026 investor reporting discloses US$15.172bn of total cumulative Brumadinho-related outlays since 2019 across a broader scope, including dam decommissioning, individual/emergency compensation and other work. That broader figure is not the cash paid under this exact 2021 agreement and must not be substituted for, added to, or currency-converted into this R$18.2bn historical observation.

cases.notes: Agreement contains both duties to perform works and duties to transfer funds. Paid figure and package overlap; they must never be added. Multi-year cash has no single valid inflation base year.

cases.matter: Exxon Valdez natural-resource restoration civil settlement
cases.disposition: 1991 court-approved civil settlement; historic Exxon Corporation predecessor, not a present-day ExxonMobil operating record

obligation.kind: 1991 settlement promise across ten-year installments, distinct from criminal fine and restitution

payment.detail: Official Exxon Valdez Oil Spill Trustee Council records the final civil settlement payment was received in September 2001. Funds were disbursed over ten years; no single inflation year can be assigned to the actual payments.

cases.notes: The separate $100m criminal restitution and $25m after-remission criminal fine are not included in the $900m civil figure. Historical Exxon successor identity is not evidence about current operations.

sources.name: Exxon Valdez Oil Spill Trustee Council — settlement and final payment received in September 2001
NOAA — 1991 Exxon Valdez civil and criminal dispositions

cases.matter: Chevron U.S.A. multistate Clean Air Act refinery settlement
cases.hazard: Air emissions, flaring, hazardous-substance release reporting
cases.disposition: Clean Air Act negotiated consent decree; parent Chevron Corporation identified in EPA corporate description

obligation.kind: Civil penalty only; excludes separately estimated pollution-control and community-project costs

payment.detail: EPA FY2007 enforcement retrospective explicitly says Chevron U.S.A. paid a $3.5m civil penalty. The exact disbursement date within the intervening period is not independently established.

cases.notes: 2003 is the announcement year used for the CPI comparator; it is not the date each penalty dollar was paid. Separate safety and pollution-control commitments must not be silently added.

sources.name: US EPA — Chevron U.S.A. Clean Air Act settlement
US EPA — FY2007 enforcement results, p.86 PDF (explicitly states paid)

cases.matter: ConocoPhillips global refinery Clean Air Act settlement
cases.hazard: Refinery NOx, SO2, VOC and benzene emissions
cases.disposition: Refinery Clean Air Act consent decree settlement

obligation.kind: Civil penalty only; separate pollution controls estimated over $525m

payment.detail: EPA documents a $4.525m penalty and future pollution-control work, but the reviewed public case summary does not establish disbursement dates or independently reconciled cash paid.

cases.notes: More than $525m in estimated equipment investment is not a confirmed cash damages payment and is excluded from the nominal penalty. Ownership of the Denver refinery later transferred to Suncor, so obligations cannot be attached to a single entity without effective dates.

sources.name: US EPA — ConocoPhillips Global Refinery Settlement

cases.matter: Passaic River cleanup engineering and design
cases.disposition: EPA consent agreement for engineering and design; corporate subsidiary, not a corporate-wide tort judgment

obligation.kind: Estimated cost of work to be performed, NOT damages paid to claimants

payment.detail: EPA describes estimated work value and future oversight costs; this source does not verify a cumulative cash disbursement under the design work commitment.

cases.notes: This estimate is a work commitment, not a cash fine or proof of quantified ecological damage. Do not equate the Occidental Chemical legal entity with every operation of Occidental Petroleum.
